crops.name: Carrots

soil.index: Aim for P and K index 3 (Teagasc). Take a soil test every 4–5 years.

conventional.lime: Lime to keep pH 6.0–7.0; apply ground limestone per soil test (typically 2.5–7.5 t/ha), ideally a few months before sowing.
conventional.manures: Account for slurry/FYM nutrients (Teagasc Green Book values) and stay within Nitrates Regulations limits (170 kg/ha organic N whole-farm; derogation rules apply).
conventional.timing: Apply P & K at or before sowing; split N to match crop demand. Observe closed periods for fertiliser and slurry.

organic.text: Avoid fresh manure (forking); use well-rotted compost to a previous crop.
organic.lime: Lime to keep pH 6.0–7.0; apply ground limestone per soil test (typically 2.5–7.5 t/ha), ideally a few months before sowing.

water.rainfall: Even moisture is key; dry–wet swings cause splitting.

harvest.storage: Lift and store cool (0–4°C) and humid, or leave in the ground under straw on light land.

conventional.pests: Carrot fly, aphids, cavity spot, Alternaria, slugs. Fleece or insecticide per label.

organic.pests: Insect-proof mesh/fleece against carrot fly, sow after the first fly generation (June), resistant varieties (e.g. Flyaway, Resistafly), rotation.
organic.weeds: Stale seedbed, pre-emergence flame weeding, close hoeing; slow to germinate so weeds compete.

crops.rotation: 1 in 4–5 years; follow a crop that received manure.
